REFERENCE BY CHAIR 
Second Anniversary of Terrorist Attack on Parliament Building on 13th 
December, 2001 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, 13th December, 2003 marks the 
Second Anniversary of the terrorist attack on the Parliament House building: 
This House recalls the heroic deed of our security personnel including two of 
the Rajya Sabha Secretariat Watch and Ward staff who lost their lives along 
with five Delhi Police personnel and a woman constable of the Central 
Reserve Police Force, while preventing entry of terrorists inside the Parliament 
House building, setting example of supreme sacrifice. One gradener of the 
C.P.W.D. has also lost his life. 
Acts of terrorism must be condemned unequivocally. On this occasion, 
we express our firm resolve to fight terrorism with determination. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in that tragedy. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)

Food for work programme in drought affected areas 
*165. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will t he Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have decided to provide work to only one -person 
in the affected family under Food for Work Scheme for people of drought affected 
areas; 
(b) if so, the rule being implemented by Government for allocation of 
foodgrains to the families having four, five or more than five members; 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
22 

(12 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) whether Government are aware of  the fact that families comprising 
more than one number are not getting  any benefit of the said scheme; 
and 
(d) if so, the action Government propose to take in this regard for 
welfare of such people? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI RAJNATH SINGH): (a) to (d) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (d)The Sampoorna Grameen RozgarYojana (SGRY) Scheme is 
implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development, with the primary objective 
of providing additional wage employment in all rural areas and thereby providing 
food security and improving nutritional levels. The Special component of 
SGRY is for augmenting food security through additional wage employment in 
the calamity affected areas. 
There was no restriction on the number of persons to be employed. 
However, the allocation of foodgrains fo r relief employment was made on the 
basis of a formula. 
For the drought of 2002-03, foodgrains were allocated to the affected States 
under the Special component of SGRY Scheme, for generation of additional 
employment, mainly to compensate for t he loss of employment in the affected 
areas. For this purpose, the States were classified into three categories and 
each household was considered of comprising of 5 members on an average. 
States which were moderately affected by drought were classified u nder 
Category "A" for whcih coverage of 20% Below Poverty Line (BPL) rural 
households was assumed for provision of employment to 1 person from each 
such rural household @ 5 kg per person per day for 10 days a month, with 
minimum of 25% of wage rate being paid in cash. Severely affected States 
were classified under Category "B" for which 50% of BPL rural households 
was assumed with other conditions remaining the same. Rajasthan was kept 
under Special category as indicated below:— 
(a) 74 worst affected blocks in the State with universal coverage of all 
willing rural households with employment to one person from each such 
rural household @ 8kg per person per day for 10 days a month with 
other conditions remaining the same; 
23 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
(b)  For all other blocks, employment @ 6 kg person per day for 10 days a 
month with other conditions remaining the same. 
However, for the later part of the dr ought (May to July 2003), a revised 
allocation for Rajasthan was approved for providing employment to all willing 
households @ 8 kg per person per day for 12 days a month. While the 
foodgrains for the severely affected States viz. Andnra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, 
Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Orissa and Rajasthan was 
provided upto July, 2003, for Tamil Nadu it was provided upto September, 
2003, as the State is mainly depende nt on North-East Monsoon (October-
December). 
The allocation formula explained above did not come in the way of 
ensuring adequate supplies of foodgrains, wherever  utilisation and actual 
employment generation justified additional allocations. 
On the basis indicated above, 87.36 lakh MTs of foodgrains, free of cost, 
were released to the drought affected States from the Special component of 
SGRY, for the drought of 2002-03. 
It is primarily the responsibility of the State Governments concerned to 
undertake all necessary measures in the wake of natural calamities including 
drought. The Central Government su pplements the effort s of the State 
Governments with financial and logistic support. Distribution of relief at the 
ground level is the responsibility of the State Governments concerned.

THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR): (a)Yes Sir. 
"Corporate Safety Plan" of Indian Railways for the period 2003 to 2013 has

(b) The Corporate Safety Plan (CSP) states the objectives, targets and 
strategies for which the Indian Railways would be striving in the next decade. The 
document encompasses the broad priorities and time frame of the safety related 
works along with assessed approximate requirement for financial investments. 
Some of the salient features of the Plan are:— 
(i)  Aim to reduce overall consequential train accidents per million train 
kilometres from 0.44 in 2002-03 to 0.17 in 2012-13. 
(ii) Targeting elimination of collisions by extensive use of Anti-Collision Device

(iii)  60% reduction in derailments.

of fireproof coaches and use of fire retardant materials in the existing 
coaches. 
(v) Containing the rising trend in level crossing accidents. 
(vi) Aiming at reduction in fatalities in  case of serious accidents by use of 
Crash Worthy Coaches and tight lock couplers with anti-climbing 
features. 
(vii) Filling up of all Safety Category posts on urgency basis. 
(viii)   Proposal for Safety Related Retirement Scheme (SRRS) for gangmen 
and drivers in age group of 50 to 57 years.

Pesticides in fruits and vegetables 
1112. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: W ill the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that according to a leading 
NGO, vegetables and fruits brought at the city's markets contain unacceptable 
level of harmful pesticides and fertilizers; 
(b) whether, according to the Foundation of Food Research and 
Enterprise to Safety and Hygiene (FRESH) every fruit and vegetable has a fair 
amount of pesticides and fertilizers, unless it comes from an orchard; and 
(c) if so, the action Government propose to take in this matter? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b)The Department is 
71 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
not aware regarding observations of Foundation of Food Research and 
Enterprise to Safety and Hygiene (FRESH) on this issue. However, according 
to the monitoring study of farm-gate and market samples of fruits and 
vegetables conducted by All India Coor dinated Research Project on Pesticide 
Residues, out of 359 samples of differ ent fruits analysed, 46% samples were 
found to contain residues of locally applied pesticides such as'e ndosulfan, 
cholorpyriphos, malathion, cypermethrin, carbendazim, mancozeb etc. 
However, in all these fruit samples, t he residues were found to be below the 
prescribed MRL values. 
Further, a total of 592 samples of  different vegetables analyzed, about 
64% were found contaminated with residues of different pesticides. However, only 
9% of the total samples contained resides above their respective MRL values. 
Pesticides residues in vegetables can be  decontaminated to 80 to 100% by 
washing and cooking. 
(c) Government of India is conc erned about the contamination of 
pesticides in fruits and vegetables and a number of steps have been taken to 
reduce the pesticides residues therein:— 
(1) Replacement of old pesticides which are required to be used in high 
dosages and which persist for a longer period in the environment with 
newer pesticide molecules, which are used in low volume and are less 
persistent in the environment; 
(2) Judicious use of pesticides being promoted through practice of 
Integrated Pest Management (IP M) which emphasizes reduced 
pesticide application; 
(3) Promotion of Organic farming; 
(4) Increased use of Bio-control agents and Bio-pesticides in agriculture as a 
replacement of chemical pesticides. 
(5) Awareness campaign through Farmers Field Schools to educate 
farmers about ill effects of pesticides and emphasis on Integrated Pest 
Management practices.

Action against companies engaged in contract farming 
†1119. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that contract farming is banned in the country; 
(b) whether Government are aware that various companies are involved 
in the work relating to contract farming in different parts of the country for last 
many years; 
(c) if so, what steps Government have taken to identify the culprit 
companies and to take action against them; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) Contract farming arrangements of different types have existed in the 
various parts of the country for centuries for both subsistence and commercial 
crops. The commercial crops like sugarc ane, cotton, tea, coffee etc. have 
always involved some forms of contract farming. Even In the case of the some 
fruit crops and fisheries, contract farming arrangements, involving mainly the 
forward trading of commodities have b een observed. Contract farming is 
becoming an increasingly important aspect of agribusiness, whether products 
are purchased by multinationals or by smaller companies. There are few 
success stories on contract farming such as Pepsico India in respect of potato, 
tomato, groundnut and chilli in Punjab, Safflower in Madhya Pradesh, oil palm in 
Andhra Pradesh, seed production contracts for hybrids seed companies etc. 
which helped the growers in realization of better returns for their produce. 
Other success stories of contract farming are milk procurement  by Amul and 
NDDB. 
(c) and (d) Since there is no ban on contract farming in the country, the 
question of taking action against contract farming companies does not arise.

food commodities are available? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir.

pesticides through Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Programme to ensure that 
pesticide residues remaining in the crop are either nil within the safe limit. For 
this purpose, about 600 Farmer Field Schools are organized by 26 Central 
Integrated Pest Management Centres at different parts of the country in a year. 
Emphasis is also given for adoption of g ood agricultural practices by farmers. 
Government is also promoting the use of  natural pesticides, biological control, 
organic farming and use of safer pesticides. Under the Insecticides Act, 1968, 
registration of bio-pesticides is encoura ged. To develop protocols for safe use 
of pesticides by recommending good agricultural practices based on 
multilocational 'supervised field trails'and to monitor pesticides residues in 
agricultural produce, Ministry of Agriculture through ICAR is already 
implementing an All India Coordinated Research Project on Pesticides 
Residues. The research findings on good agricultural practices and the simple 
methods of decontamination of pesti cide residues are promoted through

Reforming APMC  markets 
1122. SHRI R.S. GAVAI: Will the Minister of AG RICULTURE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Government have formu lated any strategy to reform 
Agriculture Produce Market Committee markets throughout the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government also propose to bring forward amendments in 
existing marketing laws and structure; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the other measures proposed to provide legal and administrative support 
for trade in various agricultural commodities? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a)   Yes, Sir. 
(b)The Inter-MinisterialTask Force on Agricultural Marketing Reforms 
constituted by this Ministry in its report of 28.6.2002 has inter-alia 
recommended that all the State Governments should amend the State 
Agricultural Produce Marketing Regulations  Act (APMC Act) to provide for the 
following: 
(i)  Enabling private   and cooperative sectors    to establish   and 
81 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
operate (including levy of service charge) agricultural marketing 
infrastructure and supporting  services. 
(ii) Direct marketing of agricultural commodities from producing areas and 
farmer's fields, without the necessity of going through licensed traders 
and regulated markets. 
(iii) Permitting "contract farming" programmes by processing or marketing 
firms. The APMC within whose jurisdiction the area covered by 
contract farming agreement lies, should record the contract farming 
agreements and act as a protector of producer's and processor's 
interests with due legal support in its jurisdiction. 
(iv) Rationalization of levy of market f ee by introducing single point levy of 
market fee in the entire process of  marketing in the State. Levy of 
market fee should be more in the na ture of service charge based on 
the quality of services provided. 
(c)The recommendations of the Task Force were discussed with the State 
Governments in the National Conference on Agricultural Marketing Reforms held 
on 27.9.2002 and later by the Standi ng Committee of State Ministers on 
29.1.2003, wherein this Ministry was requested to formulate a Model 
Legislation on Agricultural Marketing in order to guide the States in 
implementing the reforms. Accordingly, a Committee under the Chairmanship of 
Additional Secretary in the Department  of Agriculture and Cooperation has 
formulated a Model Legislation on Agricultural Marketing. 
(d) and (e)The salient features of the Model Act for State Agricultural 
Produce Marketing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2003 are as under— 
* Legal persons, growers and local authorities permitted to establish new 
markets in any area. 
* No compulsion of growers to sell their produce through existing 
regulated markets. 
* Establishment of direct purchase centres, consumers/farmers markets 
for direct sale. 
* Promotion of public private par tnership in the management and 
development of agricultural markets in the country. 
82 

[12 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
* Separate constitution for special markets for commodities like onions, 
fruits, vegetables, flowers etc. 
* A separate chapter to regulate  and promote contract farming 
arrangements in the country. 
* Prohibition of commission agency in any transaction of agricultural 
commodities with the producers. 
* Market Committee to promote altern ative marketing system, contract 
farming, direct marketing and farmers/consumers markets. 
* State Marketing Boards to promot e standardization, grading quality 
certification, market led extension and training of farmers and market 
functionaries in marketing related areas. 
* Constitution of State Marketing Standards Bureau for promotion of 
grading, standardization and quality certification of agriculture produce. 
The Model Act has been circulated  to all State Governments/UT 
Administrations for further follow up acti on as the subject matter falls within 
their purview.

National Education Policy 
†1153. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government would take any concrete steps to make 20 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
115 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
crores of students studying at primary and secondary level creative and diligent; 
(b) whether Government would formulate a National Education Policy so that 
it could be implemented uniformly in all the States and the same should remain 
consistent with each and every Government; 
(c) if so, by when, Government would take steps in this direction; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (DR. VALLABHABHAI RAMJIBHAI KATHIRIA): (a) to (d)The 
National Policy on Education (NPE) 1986, as modified in 1992, evolved on a 
national consensus, has laid down a comprehensive framework that guides the 
development of education in its entirity. The NPE provides for a National 
System of Education which implies that, upto a given level, all students, 
irrespective of caste, creed, location or sex, have access to education of a 
comparable quality. It includes a comm on education structure and a national 
curriculum framework which contains a common core alongwith other 
components, that are flexible, and envisages minimum levels of learning for each 
stage of education.The 10+2+3 structure has now been accepted in all parts of 
the country. 
MBA entrance examination 
1154. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Go vernment propose to conduct MBA* 
entrance examination from 2005 for State and private run colleges imparting 
education for MBA and post graduate management diploma programmes;  
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the candidates proposed to  be selected through this entrance 
examination will be related to the anticipated vacancies/ employment 
opportunities in these disciplines; and 
116 

[12 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (DR. VALLABHABHAI RAMJIBHAI KATHIRIA): (a) to (d)Yes, 
Sir. In pursuance of the Judgement delievered on August 14, 2003 by the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court it has been decided that the admission to all professional 
Educational Institutions (both minority and non-minority) shall be held on the basis 
of merit determined through common entrance test(s). 
For MBA/PGDM (or equivalent) programmes the admissions on all India 
basis for those institutions  that are presently holding their own entrance tests 
and admitting all their students or certain percentage of them on all India basis 
shall be made through a common all Indi a test from the academic year 2005-
06. All States shall continue to hold their own common entrance tests for 
admission to MBA/PGDM programmes in institutions within their States as 
before. 
However, these tests shall be restricted to students from within the State 
only. Students admitted on all India basis in the State level Institutions shall be 
admitted only on the basis of All India Exam. Based on the approved intake 
capacity of the management institut ions, admissions shall be given to 
candidates. 
Marketing of projects of IIT, Kanpur 
1155.  SHRI R.P. GOENKA: 
MISS MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of useful inventions and 
technologies developed by the scientists at the Indian Institute of Technology, 
Kanpur and other such prestigious institutes have not been allowed to make a 
transition to the market, but are only st acked in the archieves or recorded in 
journals, due to reported bureaucratic inadequate evaluation of the new device or 
technology for its marketability; 
117 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
(b) if so, the details of such known cases; and 
(c) the steps being taken for better coordination with the scientific 
fraternity to ensure marketing of the projects after their completion? 
THE MINISTER OF ST ATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (DR. VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI KATHIRIA): (a) and (b) 
No, Sir. Rather several of the technologies developed at IIT, Kanpur have been 
very well appreciated by the industry and have been or are in the process of being 
commercially utilized. Some of these are:- 
(i) Development of saddlery moulds and saddlery trees. Earlier these moulds 
were imported at a cost of appr oximately Rs. 3,000/-each whereas 
with this development, these can be locally produced for Rs. 600/-. 
About 20,000 of these trees using three moulds have been supplied to 
the industrial units in Kanpur. 
(ii) The technology developed for detecting the flatness of wheel of railway 
vehicle has been successfully tested between Kanpur-Lucknow 
sector. The Railways will now extend this to other sectors. 
(iii) An operating system has been developed for smart card for transport 
applications. This system has be en certified and accepted as a 
standard by the Government of India. 
(iv) An MoU has been signed with industry for utilisation of the technology 
developed for power distribution aut omation under the Technology 
Development Mission. 
(v) The software developed for translation of Hindi to English and English 
to Hindi has been transferred, on a non-exclusive basis, to two 
organizations. 
(vi) An electrochemical deep hole drilling machine is being developed in 
collaboration with a major public sector organisation. 
(c)To nurture technological innovations, IIT, Kanpur in collaboration with 
SIDBI has set up the SIDBI, Innovation and Incubation Centre.

Revenue sharing by RailTel Corporation 
1199. SHRIMATI KAMLA MANHAR: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the RailTel Corporation has decided to offer telecom 
bandwidth to optical fibre cable along its 62,000 km. Track network; 
(b) whether RailTel has also decided to follow revenue sharing model with 
Cable TV operators; and 
(c) if so, the complete details thereof and to what extend the RailTel will be 
benefited from these projects? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI 
BASANGOUDA R. PATIL): (a) Yes, Sir. RailTel Corporation of India Limited (RailTel) 
is offering bandwidth on sale/lease to Telecom service providers, wherever Optical 
Fibre Cable (OFC) based communication network has been installed along the 
Railway track.

to leasing of dark fibres/bandwidth to Cable TV operators. Decision to adopt 
one or other scheme is on case to case and demand basis. 
(c) RailTel has leased dark fibre in Mumbai area to one Cable TV 
operator on revenue sharing basis. In th is case, the revenue stream has two 
components — A fixed component on the basis of length of the fibre leased and 
a variable component on the basis of number of cable TV subscribers served 
by the Operator in that area. In Kolk ata area, however, the revenue stream 
has a fixed component only, depending upon the length of the fibre leased. 
RailTel may also sell bandwidth to Cable operators to extend signal from 
one centre to other, if such a demand arises in future. 
Policy on the revenue sharing model will be firmed up after gaining of 
some experience in this business. 
Extending different kind of services to cable TV operators is a new source 
of income to RailTel and this definitel y will benefit RailTel in improving its 
financial prospects.

till October, 2003? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI 
BASANGOUDA R. PATIL): (a) No, Sir. However, certain irregularities involving 
wrong classification and overloading in transportation of goods and involving 
accountal in disposal of scrap have been detected by the vigilance.

detect cases of wrong classification and overloading in the area of 
transportation of goods. In addition to existing mechanical weighbridges,

detect incidences of evasion of revenue and to curb the malpractices. To 
strengthen the system of accountal of scrap, electronic weighbridges have been

addition to above, accountal of rail and the permanent way material is being 
computerized.

detected irregularities in the matter of wrong classification and overloading in 
transportation of goods amounting to Rs . 33.6 crores during the period from

irregularities amounting to Rs. 27.4 cr ores during the pe riod from January,

Price index 
1215. SHRI SURESH PACHOURI: W ill the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that during the last three years the price index of 
foodgrains have remained almost stat ionery while the price index of all 
commodities has gone up by 14.6 per cent;

(c) the steps taken by Government to improve the rural economy? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b ) According to the Wholesale 
Price Index (WPI) with base 1993-94=100 the WPI of foodgrains declined by 
1.2% during 1999-2000 to 2002-2003 while WPI of all commodities increased by 
14.8% during the same period.The reason for the marginal decline in the prices 
of foodgrains can be traced to the comfortable stock position of rice and wheat 
coupled with remarkable increase in production of foodgrains during both 
years 1999-2000 and 2001 -2002, whic h ensured adequate availability of 
foodgrains in the country. As regards the increase in the WPI of all commodities, it 
may be noted that the WPI in respect of the major group "fuel, power, light and 
lubricants" increased by 47.7% during the period 1999-2000—2002-2003 while 
the WPI in respect of the major group "manufactured products" increased by 
7.9% during this period. The WPI for the broad group "primary articles" 
increased by 10.1% during the same period. Though WPI for the sub-group 
"foodgrains" forms a part of primary articles, its share in the weight of the broad 
group "primary articles" is relatively low and hence the decline in the prices of 
foodgrains during 1999-2000— 2002-2003 was more than offset by the 
increase in the prices of other items in the broad group of primary articles.

farmers will have to resort to new bio-technological developments; and

TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TE CHNOLOGY (SHRI 
BACHI SINGH RAWAT): (a) Yes, Sir. In a recently held workshop on the Role of

continue to play a significant role in sustainable food security of the 
197

country in the future. Apart from increasing the yield, biotechnology has a great 
potential in enhancing nutritive value of food crops. India can benefit from this 
frontier technology both in terms of increased production and enhanced nutritional 
quality crops. The Department of Biotechn ology as well as Indian Council of 
Agricultural Research independently and in collaboration have initiated several 
research and development activities in this direction. The National Agricultural 
Research System is also addressing mo st of the concerns for meeting the 
food and nutritional dem and of the ever-growing population through indigenous 
development of transgenics in various crops especially to address the problem 
of tolerance to biotic/abiotic st resses. To strengthen research in 
biotechnological application in agriculture, Government is putting renewed thrust

(ii) Schemes of Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports implemented by NYKS in 
Uttar Pradesh during last three years (2000-2003) 
210 

[12 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
1. National Service Volunteers 
The primary objective of NSV scheme is to provide opportunities to those 
graduate students below 25 years of age who feel motivated to serve the 
community for a year or two. Each volunteer is paid an honorarium of Rs. 
1000/- p.m. 1911 NSVs were with the NYKS and their services were utilized 
by the Kendras. 
2. Youth Development Centres 
The main objective of this scheme is the overall development of the rural 
youth in the country through the inst rumentality of a Youth Development 
Centre (YDC) which would serve a cluster of 10 villages. The YDC is to function 
as a centre of information, training and development of sports for the youth in the 
rural areas. One time financial assistance of Rs. 30,000/- is given to each YDC. 
22 Youth Development Centres were established during last three years. 
3. Awards to Outstanding Youth Clubs 
The objective of the scheme is to encourage the growth of Youth Clubs 
which have been recognized as catalyst of social change. The award money 
at district level is Rs. 10 ,000/-, at the state level is Rs. 15,000 and at National 
level Rs. 100,000, 50,000, 25,000 for 1st, llnd, lllrd position respectively. 48 
Awards were conferred during last three years. 
4. Financial Assistance to Youth Clubs 
The main philosophy behind this cheme is to encourage newly 
established Youth Clubs. Under this scheme assistance to the tune of Rs. 
10,000 per Youth Club for normal area and Rs. 15000 per  Youth Clubs for tribal 
areas is being given to such youth clubs which are registered under Societies 
Registration Act 1860 or Corresponding State Act. 163 Youth Clubs -were 
assisted under the scheme during last three years. 
5. Rural Sports Clubs 
The principal objective of this scheme is to help the emergence of a 
countrywide network of Sports Club Cult ure for canalizing the energies of 
youth for constructive activities on one hand and exploring 
211 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
and nurturing sports talent in rural and tribal areas on the others. Budget to the tune 
of Rs. 30,000 (normal area) and Rs. 45,000 (tribal area) are earmarked for each such 
club. 25 Rural Sports Club were established during the last three years. 
(iii) Special Programmes organized in Uttar Pradesh during last three years 
(2000-2003) 
1. Swamjayanti Gram Swarojgar Yojana-A Rural Youth Initiative 
Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan with the financial support from the Ministry of Rural 
Development, Government of India has undertaken a project named Swamjayanti 
Gram Swarojgar Yojana-A Rural Youth Initiative in selected 8 districts in first phase and 
6 more district were added in second phase during the year 2002-03. This is a Pilot 
Project out of which 14000 poor people are expected to get benefit. The objective of the 
project is to organize the poor from below poverty line (BPL) families in self-help 
groups and to build their capacities so that they at their own can start income 
generating ventures. In each district 100 Self Help groups were formed. The selected 
districts are Nalbari and Kamrup (Assam); Gumla (Jharkhand); Vaishali (Bihar); Nellore 
(Andhra Pradesh) Hamirpur (Uttar Pr adesh); Jagatsingpur and Kalahandi 
(Orissa); Bhopal; Dewas, Sehore (Madhya Pradesh), Sarguja (Chhattisgarh) 
and Chamoli (Uttaranchal). 
During' the year 2002-03 in the first project of eighth districts activities like 
thrift and credit programme for SHGs, Grading of SHGs, Distribution of Revolving fund, 
preparation of project proposal for SHGS and Skill Development Training of SHGs etc. 
were conducted. The Second project .was started during the year 2002-03 and 
activities including orientation training to key project implementers, formation of district 
level committee, selection of supervisors and motivators, selection of Blocks and 
villages, Training supervisors and motivators, motivational Campaign and PRA 
were conducted. 
Hamirpur district has been identified in Uttar Pradesh under this SGSY scheme in 
which 44 villages were covered. 100 SHGs have been formulated and out of which 50 SHGs 
got Revolving Fund. 2 Supervisors and 20 Motivators were deployed. 
212 

[12 December, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
2. Deen Dayal Upadhyay Swavlamban Yojana Project 
NYKS started a new project entitled Deen Dayal Upadhyay Swavlamban 
Yojana Project in 12 selected districts of six States of the country. Project was 
inaugurated by Hon'ble Shri L.K. Advani, Deputy Prime Minister of India on 12th July, 
2002. Selected district are Karvi Anglong and Kamrup (Assam), Gumla and Simdega 
(Jharkhand), Bhopal, Sehore, Tikamgam and Chhattrapur (Madhya Pradesh) Phoolbani (Orissa) 
and Lalitpur, Jhansi and Mathura (Uttar Pradesh).The project is aimed at motivating the 
youth to form Self Help Groups so that they may undertake income generating activities and 
gainful employment. During the year 2002-03 activities related to deployment of Project 
Officer, Orientation training to Key project implementer, selection of motivators, formation 
of district level committee, training of supervisors and motivators, capacity building 
programme and formation of Self-Help Group were organized. 
Under this scheme, three district namely Mathura, Jhansi and Lalitpur has been 
selected. 15 villages were covered in each district. More than, 30 SHG were formulated, 
three Project officers and 15 motivators were deployed in each identified district of Uttar 
Pradesh. 
3. Villagers Talk AIDS (VTA) 
NYKS in collaboration with Naitonal AIDS Control Organization (NACO) is 
implementing VillagersTalk AIDS(VTA) Project in 385 districts of the country. The objective of 
the project is to generate mass awareness among masses especially the rural youth about 
sexuality, HIV-AIDS and prevention techniques; to make HIV-AIDS awareness 
generation programmes and campaigns through self-sustaining local youth initiative, 
participation and leadership and to prevent and stop the spread of HIV-AIDS infection. As 
on dateljnder the project following activities were organized:— 
The project was implemented in 1500 villages of 50 districts of Uttar Pradesh. 
Under this project, a total of 3,000 rural youth named Conveners and Joint Conveners 
were identified, selected and trained not only for their empowerment to protect members 
for HIV infection but also to spearhead the local planning process and undertake the 
project activities on a sustainable basis. As a part of the process, all the Regional 
Coordinators and Youth Coordinators of NYKS were oriented in a two 
213 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
days Orientation Programme. It was followed by the organization of 100 training 
programme for all the identified Conveners and Joint Conveners. For the 
implementation of the project, funds to the tune of Rs. 45,100/-were released for 
the district level activities viz. Youth Leadership Training Programme, Awareness 
Campaigns, Exhibitions and Focus Group Discussions. Under this project, 100 
Youth Leadership Training Programmes, 200 Awareness Generation 
Programmes, 150 Focus Group Discussions and 200 Exhibitions were organized. 
A total of 650 activities were organized and 75,000 youths were directly 
benefited. 
4. Tenzing Norgey Adventure Camp 
This camp has been established by NYKS at Dehradun (Uttaranchal) with an 
objective to promote the spirit of adv enture sports and love for fellow living 
being and mother land besides providing an unique platform for the rural youth 
whereby they may be provided air, water and surface adventure activities under 
single umbrella.Through this programme, 1522 odd youth have been trained 
through 24 Camps in Trekking, Mountaineering, Rock Climbing, Redling, 
Water Surfing, Parasailing, Mountain Biking. 
5. Kashmiri Rural Youth Cultural Exchange Programme 
NYKS has undertaken this programme in collaboration with Ministry of Home 
Affairs, with the objective to arrange educational and awareness tour programmes 
for the youth from the Kashmir Valley to other parts of the country. A total of 25 
batches each batch with the strength of  33 youth have been taken on circuit 
tour under this programme. A total of  825 Youth have been benefited under 
this programme during the last three years. 
6. South East Asian Flame for Freedom from Tobacco (SEAAT 
Flame) 
NYKS in collaboration with WHO and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
has undertaken a programme of SE AAT Flame. The SEAAT Flame was 
accompanied by a group of artists and youth leader. The SEAAT Flame 
travelled to about 150 districts of the country. En-route, it spread the message 
among the people particularly the youth about harmful effects of tobacco 
consumption. 
SEAAT Flame was flagged off by Shri C.P. Thakur, Hon'ble Minister of 
Health and Family Welfare, Government of India on

31st May, 2003 at New Delhi. The Flame was taken through the State of Delhi, 
Haryana, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya 
Pradesh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh in firs: phase. In Second phase 
SEAAT flame was started from Bhubaneshwar Orissa on 19th July, 2002 which 
was flagged off by Shri Surat Kumar Kar, Hon'ble Speaker, Orissa Vidhan 
Sabha. SEAAT Flame traveller through the States of Orissa, West Bengal, 
Bihar, Assam, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi. The closing function was organised on 
5th September, 2002 at New Delhi where Shri Vikram Verma, Hon'b'o Minister 
of Youth Affairs and Sports was the Chief Guest. 
7. World No Tobacco Day 
NYKS in collaboration wi th WHO and Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare has undertaken the above programme with an objective to make youth 
aware of the hazardous consequenc es of tobacco consumption. The 
programme was dedicated to Tobacco Free Sports. Programme was organised 
on World No Tobacco Day 31.5.2002. 
Under this programme 34 States and one National Level Programme were 
organised. The main function of World No Tobacco Day was organized at National 
Stadium New Delhi on 31 st May, 2002. The Programme was formally launched 
by the Chief Guest, Hon'ble Shri C.P.Thakur, Union Minister of Health and 
Family Welfare, Government of India. In all the State capitals programme and 
rallies were organised for making youth aware of the harmful use of the tobacco. 
A total of 26348 youths were directly benefited through this programme.

Assistance to Karnataka for golf-club 
1229. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Karnataka Government has sought financial assistance for 
developing a golf-club at Chickmanglur under Large Revenue Generating Project; 
and 
(b) if so, the details in this regard and the Centre's reaction thereto? 
217 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2003] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (SHRI VIJAY GOEL): (a) and (b) No proposal seeking financial 
assistance for development of Golf Club at Chickmangalur from the Karnataka 
Government has been received. However, Ministry of Tourism and Culture had 
forwarded the proposal from Chickmangalur Golf Club, Karnataka during January, 
2001 for development of Golf Course in Chickm angalur. Since there was no 
provision under the scheme of Grants for Creation of Sports Infrastructure for 
rendering of Central assistance for development of golf course, the proposal 
could not be considered for assistance. Ministry of Tourism and Culture was 
informed accordingly on 9.2.2001. 
Anti-doping measures vis-a-vis use of THG 
1230. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that tetrahydro-gestrinone (THG) 
manufactured by Bay Area Laboratory, similar to anabolic steriods, is 
alleged to be used by Indian Sports persons; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps taken for effective anti-doping test measures in India? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (SHRI VIJAY GOEL): (a) and (b) No , Sir. No such instances of use 
by Indian Sports persons has come to Government's notice. 
(c) In the present scenario, the Anti Doping Programme is managed by 
Sports Authority of India (SAI) through a centrally sponsored scheme of Govt, of 
India Called "Scheme for Dope Test". 
SAI has a Dope Control Centre (DCC) located at Jawaharlal Nehru 
Stadium, New Delhi. DCC got ISO 9001 : 2000 and ISO; 17025 certification 
which are mandatory requirements as per International Olympic Committee 
(IOC) norms for seeking permanent accreditation for the DCC. After achieving 
ISO: 17025 Certification. The DCC, SAI has achieved another milestone by 
getting temporary accreditation from International Olympic Committee/World 
Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) for testing of atheltes" samples during the 1st 
Afro Asian Games.

Inspection of facilities for Commonwealth Games 
1232. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:  
SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD: 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Commonwelath Authorities had visited India 
recently to oversee the facilities for allo wing Indian to eventually allow bidding 
for the forthcoming Commonwealth Games; 
(b) if so, which is the venue city, Government have decided to bid for hosting 
the Commonwealth Games; and 
(c) the details of result of the visit of Commonwealth Authorities to India? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (SHRI VIJAY GOEL): (a) Yes, Sir. A team of the Commonwealth 
Games Federation visited Delhi on 3—7 August, 2003 to assess India's 
preparedness for hosting the 2010 Commonwealth Games. 
(b) and (c)The venue city for Commonwealth Games, 2010 is Delhi. 
Subsequent to the visit of the team and submission of its report to the 
Commonwealth Games Federation, the General Assembly meeting of the 
Commonwealth Games Federation was held at Montego Bay (Jamaica) on 13 
November, 2003 and Delhi, India was given the rights for hosting of the 
Commonwealth Games, 2010.
